rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators take the person in darkness to be the disbeliever, immersed in unbelief and error.
rows.anchor: الظلمات}. قال المفسرون: (يعني: الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording can mean simply one in darkness: Arabic may add mathal without intending comparison, as in the cited constructions and verses 5:95 and 42:11.
rows.anchor: ولا يريدون به التشبيه، كقولهم: أنا أكرم مثلك

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Another reading says the person's likeness is in darkness, so he too is in darkness; the intended referent is the disbeliever himself, not his likeness.
rows.anchor: المراد به: الكافر لا شبيهه، وهذان القولان معنى ما ذكره أبو علي

rows.speaker: غيره من النحويين
rows.claim: Other grammarians say mathal is added because the wording makes the person an example of being in darkness.
rows.anchor: معنى الآية: كمن في الظلمات، وزيد المثل لأنه يفيد أنه يضرب به المثل في ذلك

rows.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
rows.claim: He parses it as someone whose likeness would be likened to one in darkness; al-Wahidi calls this the weakest explanation.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسين بن الفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says mithl and mathal have the same meaning here.
rows.anchor: يمشي به كمن هو في الظلمات

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses being unable to leave the darkness as never becoming a believer.
rows.anchor: ليس بخارج منها}. قال الكلبي: (ليس بمؤمن أبدا)

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators agree that the verse was revealed about a believer and a disbeliever, and identify Abu Jahl as the disbeliever.
rows.anchor: واتفق المفسرون على أن هذه الآية نزلت في مؤمن وكافر، وأجمعوا على أن الكافر أبو جهل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the believer as Hamza: after Abu Jahl insulted Muhammad, Hamza confronted him and declared faith, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: حمزة بن عبد المطلب، وذلك أن أبا جهل رمى النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بفرث

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid says the verse concerns Muhammad and Abu Jahl: Abu Jahl rejected Muhammad out of tribal rivalry and demanded revelation for himself; the account also links 6:124.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: (نزلت في النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأبي جهل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: On the report identifying Muhammad and Abu Jahl, Muhammad received guidance, Islam's light, prophethood, and wisdom, while Abu Jahl remained in unbelief's darkness.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: (على هذا القول فالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - هدى

rows.speaker: عكرمة والكلبي
rows.claim: Ikrima and al-Kalbi identify the believer as Ammar ibn Yasir and the disbeliever as Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة (¬7) والكلبي (¬8): (نزلت في عمار بن ياسر، وأبي جهل)

rows.speaker: الضحاك ويمان
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Yaman identify the believer as Umar ibn al-Khattab and the disbeliever as Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك (¬9)، ويمان: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse is general and was not revealed about any particular believer and disbeliever.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن (¬1): (الآية عامة [في كل مؤمن وكافر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj likewise allows a general reading: every guided person is like the dead revived and lit among people by wisdom and faith, while every disbeliever is trapped in darkness.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج: (يجوز أن تكون هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Satan made idol worship attractive to the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: زين الشيطان لهم عبادة الأصنام)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison means their unbelief was made attractive and they acted on it, just as faith was made attractive to the believers; their cases are likened in this adornment.
rows.anchor: فشبهت حال هؤلاء في التزيين بحال أولئك فيه

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq assigns the kāf the syntactic position of nominative: the meaning is that the like of what was recounted was made attractive to the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: موضع الكاف رفع، المعنى: مثل ذلك الذي قصصنا عليك زين للكافرين عملهم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators understand the verse as jinn and humans gathered together at the resurrection's assembly place.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬4): (يعني: الجن والإنس يجمعون في موقف

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas as identifying those gathered as the jinn and their satan companions.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (يريد: هم وقرناؤهم من الشياطين)

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj supplies an implied introductory phrase: they are addressed with, It will be said to them, O company of jinn.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: (المعنى: فيقال لهم: {يا معشر الجن}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Qatada explain the jinn's having taken many humans as their having led them astray through seduction and misguidance.
rows.anchor: من إغواء الإنس وإضلالهم، عن ابن عباس (¬8)، والحسن (¬9)، وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والفراء
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas's tafsir, the phrase means that the jinn led many humans astray; al-Farra gives the same explanation.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس في

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as the many people whom the jinn caused to go astray.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: (كثر من أغويتم منهم)

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq reads it as the many humans whom the jinn misled.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: ({قد استكثرتم} ممن أضللتموه من الإنس)

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another commentator states explicitly that the jinn gained many humans through seduction and misguidance; al-Wahidi says the explanations amount to the same thing.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: ({قد استكثرتم من الإنس} بالإغواء والإضلال)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humans called the jinn's allies are the people whom the jinn led astray.
rows.anchor: الذين أضلوهم من الإنس

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج والكلبي وعكرمة
rows.claim: These authorities describe humans seeking a valley jinn's protection while traveling in desolate country; humans gain safety, while jinn gain the honor of being treated as powerful protectors.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن (¬3) وابن جريج (¬4)، والكلبي (¬5)، وعكرمة

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج والكلبي وعكرمة
rows.claim: In this account, a jinn boasts that humans and jinn have submitted to him, since a human has acknowledged his ability to protect him.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن (¬3) وابن جريج (¬4)، والكلبي (¬5)، وعكرمة (¬6)

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن جريج والكلبي وعكرمة
rows.claim: They cite 72:6 as evidence for humans seeking refuge with jinn.
rows.anchor: واحتجوا على هذا بقوله تعالى: {وأنه كان رجال من الإنس يعوذون برجال من الجن}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's report, says the mutual enjoyment occurred in worldly life and involved the jinn leading humans astray.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: {ربنا استمتع بعضنا ببعض}: (يريد: في الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
rows.claim: On this explanation, jinn enjoyed human obedience to their calls toward error, unbelief, and sins; humans enjoyed jinn's beautifying desired acts and making them easier.
rows.anchor: أن استمتاع الجن بالإنس طاعتهم لهم فيما يغرونهم به من الضلالة والكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the mutual-misguidance explanation: the wording points to humans accepting jinn's temptations, and few humans sought refuge with jinn.
rows.anchor: اختيار الزجاج؛ لأنه قال: (الذي يدل عليه

rows.speaker: الحسن والسدي وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Suddi, and most commentators take the appointed term to mean death.
rows.anchor: في قول الحسن (¬2) والسدي (¬3)، وأكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the appointed term to be resurrection and gathering.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو البعث والحشر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses mathwākum as your place of staying.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: فيها مقامكم)

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says mathwā means abode and khālidīn is an accusative circumstantial qualifier: the Fire is their abode while they remain there eternally.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: (المثوى: المقام، {خالدين فيها} منصوب على الحال

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali argues mathwā is a verbal noun, not a place noun, because the following circumstantial phrase operates on it; it means the Fire is your remaining there, with the addressees as semantic agents.
rows.anchor: المثوى عندي في الآية اسم للمصدر دون المكان، لحصول الحال في الكلام معملا فيها

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali adduces poetry where maghār takes an object introduced by ʿalā; this shows it is a verbal noun, while a place noun would not govern an object.
rows.anchor: وما هي إلا في إزار وعلقة

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains time adverbials such as the cited expressions as verbal nouns used by extension after deleting a time noun; their sense of passing suits time.
rows.anchor: فهو من باب قولك: أتيتك خفوق النجم، ومقدم الحاج، وخلافة فلان

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali notes that Arabic often uses mā with a verb as a time adverbial, and some grammarians call this construction mā of time.
rows.anchor: حتى إن قوما من النحويين (¬5) يسمونها ما

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali understands the people addressed as those who deserve to dwell and remain eternally in the Fire; Ibn Abbas's gloss of mathwā as a place of staying supports this.
rows.anchor: وقول ابن عباس: (فيها مقامكم)

words: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the exception covers people already known by God to accept Islam and believe the Prophet and his message; this requires mā to mean man, those who.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (استثنى الله قوما قد سبق في علمه

words: خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq takes the exception from the duration of Judgment Day: it excludes the time spent being raised from graves and being judged before entry into the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (معنى الاستثناء عندي: إنما هو من يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God decreed faith, repentance, and truthful belief for the excepted people, and knew the goodness, piety, and faith in their hearts.
rows.anchor: حكم للذين استثنى بالتصديق والتوبة وعلم ما في قلوبهم من البر والتقوى والإيمان

words: يَٰمَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ قَدِ ٱسْتَكْثَرْتُم مِّنَ ٱلْإِنسِ
rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The people of meaning read the passage as a warning against jinn tempting people and making evil attractive, since the jinn and their human allies will be paired in the Fire.
rows.anchor: معنى هذه الآية: التحذير من إغواء الجن تزيينهم القبيح، فإنهم يقرنون مع أوليائهم من الإنس في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi lists forms ظفر with fāʾ vowelled or quiescent, reports Hasan's kasra on ẓāʾ with quiescent fāʾ, and Abu al-Sammal's kasra on both; أظفور is another form, attested in poetry.
rows.anchor: في الظفر لغات: ظفر بضم الفاء وهو أعلاها، وظفر بسكون الفاء، وظفر بكسر الظاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid identify the forbidden animals as camels and ostriches; al-Zajjaj prefers this explanation, and Ibn Abbas says ostriches have nails like camels.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: (هو البعير والنعامة) (¬2)، وهو قول مجاهد (¬3)، واختيار الزجاج

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada defines the prohibition broadly as every creature whose toes are not split.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: (كل ذي ظفر ليس بمشقوق الأصابع)

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj lists camel, ostrich, duck, goose, and wild ass as unsplit-footed and forbidden, contrasting them with split-footed fowl such as chicken and sparrows.
rows.anchor: كل ذي ظفر لم يفرج قوائمه من البهائم كالبعير والنعامة والبط والأوز

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Muslim says the phrase means birds with talons and beasts with hooves; calling the hoof a nail is metaphorical, as poetry calls it a foot.
rows.anchor: أي: كل ذي مخلب من الطير، وكل ذي حافر من الدواب

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم
rows.claim: Abd Allah ibn Muslim cites poetry describing a hoof as a foot to support the figurative use of nail for hoof.
rows.anchor: فجعل الحافر موضع القدم

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس وابن زيد
rows.claim: Ata's report from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd restricts the forbidden animal to camels alone.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء، عن ابن عباس: (يريد: الإبل) (¬3)، وهو قول ابن زيد

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators identify the forbidden fats as the omenta and kidney fats; Ibn Abbas calls them the internal fats.
rows.anchor: المفسرون: (يعني: الثروب (¬5) وشحم الكليتين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says fat attached to the animals' backs was excluded from the prohibition.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (إلا ما علق بالظهر من الشحم فإني لم أحرمه)

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada includes fat attached to the back and side from within the animals' bellies.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: (ما علق بالظهر والجنب من داخل بطونهما)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hawāyā means the bowels and intestines; its singular forms include hāwiya, ḥawiya, and ḥawiyāʾ.
rows.anchor: الحوايا} وهي المباعر والمصارين، واحدتها حاوية

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi defines the word as the circular coil in a sheep's belly.
rows.anchor: هي الحوية والحاوية، وهي الدوارة التي في بطن الشاة

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit gives hāwiya and ḥawiya as singulars of ḥawāyā, compares the pattern with zawiya/zawāyā and rāwiya/rawāyā, and records hāwiyāʾ as another singular.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: (يقال: حاوية وحوايا مثل زاوية وزوايا

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit also records ḥawiya for the pack-like saddle placed on a camel's back for riding.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من يقول: حوية وحوايا مثل الحوية التي توضع على ظهر البعير ويركب فوقها

rows.speaker: جرير
rows.claim: Jarir's verse uses ḥāwiyāʾ in describing the place where small reptiles feed, as poetic evidence for the word.
rows.anchor: وأنشد قول جرير: تضغو الخنانيص والغول التي أكلت

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari cites a verse using ḥawāyāʾ in a comparison with the hissing of snakes and scorpions.
rows.anchor: كأن نفيق الحب في حاويائه

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali gives three possible singulars and explains that the plural is fawāʿil from hāwiya/hāwiyāʾ or faʿāʾil from ḥawiya; the latter passes through ḥawāʾi before sound change.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: (الحوايا واحدتها حوية وحاوياء

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains that ḥawāʾi becomes ḥawāyā: a final yāʾ preceded by kasra shifts to alif, and the hamza shifts to yāʾ to avoid adjacent similar letters; compare the hamza discussion at 7:10.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: (الحوايا واحدتها حوية وحاوياء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the exception means what the intestines carried; Ibn Abbas's gloss treats the intestines and what is mixed with bone as fat left unprohibited.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: (أرادوا ما حملت الحوايا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi parses al-hawāyā as coordinated with the subject backs in the nominative.
rows.anchor: عطف على الظهور في موضع رفع

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra allows an accusative parse by ellipsis: understand fat of the intestines, deleting fat as in the command to ask the town, meaning its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب بتقدير حذف المضاف على أن تريد أو شحوم الحوايا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra confirms that ḍawʿ is coordinated with naʾīm, not al-būm, just as al-hawāyā is coordinated with mā, not the backs.
rows.anchor: يذهب إلى أن الضوع عطف على النئيم، ولم يعطف على البوم كما عطفت (الحوايا) على ما

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: All commentators identify what is mixed with bone as the fat of the tail.
rows.anchor: يعني: شحم الألية، في قول جميع المفسرين

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj includes fat in the limbs, flank, head, eyes, and ears, which people deemed permissible as mixed with bone; only omentum and kidney fat were prohibited.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: (كل شحم في القوائم والجنب والرأس

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra parses mā as an accusative coordinated with the earlier exception, what the backs carried; this is the majority exegetical analysis.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: (و (ما) في موضع نصب نسقا على ما في الأولى

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq reports an alternative parse: intestines and fat mixed with bone coordinate with the prohibited fats, while only what the backs carried is excepted and permitted.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (قال قوم: حرمت عليهم الثروب، وأحل لهم ما حملت الظهور

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq says aw here broadly marks items each worthy of the prohibition or permission in question; unlike wa, it makes clear that any one or all listed items fit the instruction.
rows.anchor: وأو بليغة في هذا المعنى؛ لأنك إذا قلت: لا تطع زيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi explains that this prohibition was their recompense for transgression.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ذلك} أي: ذلك التحريم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Mujahid specifies their transgression as killing prophets, taking usury, and wrongfully appropriating people's property.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: (عقوبة لهم بقتلهم الأنبياء

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi calls it punishment for their sins and links it to 4:160, where good things were forbidden to the Jews for their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: ({جزيناهم ببغيهم} عاقبناهم بذنوبهم، نظيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is truthful in reporting both the prohibition and the Jews' transgression.
rows.anchor: أي: في الإخبار عن التحريم وعن بغيهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the earth in which people live as the earth of this world.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: الأرض أرض الدنيا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says the pronoun returns to the preceding statement that people have an abode on earth in 7:24.
rows.anchor: والكناية عائدة إلى قوله: {ولكم في الأرض مستقر}

words: فِيهَا تَحْيَوْنَ وَفِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ
rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi explains that people live and are buried in the earth, then emerge from their graves from the earth for resurrection.
rows.anchor: في الأرض تعيشون، وفي الأرض قبوركم، ومن الأرض تخرجون من قبوركم للبعث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says their disobedience to the Lord of the worlds brought them abandonment by God.
rows.anchor: يريد: بعصيانهم رب العالمين خذلوا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says their persistent disobedience made their trial more severe.
rows.anchor: أي: شددت عليهم المحنة بفسقهم

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: The commentators divide the town into Sabbath fishers and eaters, a group that forbade and rebuked them, and a group that refrained from fishing and questioned the admonishers.
rows.anchor: افترق أهل القرية ثلاث فرق؛ فرقة صادت وأكلت، وفرقة نهت وزجرت

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the quiet group blamed the admonishers because they knew the offenders would not stop; the admonishers replied that enjoining right was their duty and an excuse before God.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: (لاموهم على موعظة قوم يعلمون أنهم غير مقلعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿdhira is a verbal noun like ʿudhr.
rows.anchor: والمعذرة مصدر كالعذر

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd gives the forms ʿadhartuhu, aʿdhiruhu, ʿudhran, maʿdhiratan, and ʿudhrā for excusing someone.
rows.anchor: عذرته أعذره عذرا ومعذرة وعذرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root means to stand up for or accept someone's excuse; the admonishers say their warning will let them answer God that they performed their duty and are excused.
rows.anchor: ومعنى عذره في اللغة (¬4): قام بعذره، وقبل

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azhari calls maʿdhira a noun on the mafʿila pattern standing for an act of apology, as though the speakers said their admonition is an apology to God.
rows.anchor: المعذرة اسم على مفعلة من عذر يعذر، وأقيم مقام الاعتذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi points to the related expression in 9:66, previously discussed in the chapter on repentance.
rows.anchor: {لا تعتذروا قد كفرتم} الآية

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi says ʿudhr, ʿudhrā, and maʿdhira can mean an exit from blame or sin.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: (يقال: لي في هذا الأمر عذر

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says they did not offer a new excuse for an alleged offense; asked why they admonished, they answered that their admonition itself was an excuse.
rows.anchor: لم يريدوا أن يعتذروا عذرا مستأنفا من أمر ليموا عليه، ولكنهم قيل لهم

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says a speaker would put maʿdhira in the accusative in the construction, I offer an excuse to God and to you regarding such-and-such.
rows.anchor: لو قال رجل لرجل: معذرة إلى الله، وإليك من كذا وكذا لنصب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj supplies the omitted verb: the meaning is, we offer an excuse.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬7): (المعنى: نعتذر معذرة)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonishers considered it possible that their warning would benefit the offenders, so that they might fear God and stop transgressing.
rows.anchor: أي: جائز عندنا أن ينتفعوا بالمعذرة فيتقوا الله ويتركوا العدو

rows.speaker: الكلبي والزجاج
rows.claim: A second account has only two groups, the admonishers and the offenders; on this account, those asking why they admonish are the offenders.
rows.anchor: وكانوا فرقتين: فرقة نهت عن السوء، وفرقة عملت بالسوء

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the offenders numbered about seventy thousand and the admonishers about twelve thousand; the offenders asked why they warned if punishment was already known to be near.
rows.anchor: المعتدية نحو من سبعين ألفا أتاهم طوائف نحو من اثني عشر ألفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi prefers the three-group account: if the admonishers spoke to offenders directly, the pronoun should be laʿallakum, you may fear God, not laʿallahum, they may fear God.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول (¬6) أصح؛ لأنهم لو كانوا فرقتين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses forgetting the warning as leaving what they had been admonished to do.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (أي: تركوا ما وعظوا به)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those rescued are the group that forbade evil.
rows.anchor: {أنجينا الذين ينهون عن السوء}، يعني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء بن السائب
rows.claim: In one report, Ibn Abbas suspends judgment about the silent group: the verse mentions the people who forbade evil but does not say what happened to those who asked why they admonished.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء بن السائب (¬2): (أسمع الله يقول

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another report, Ibn Abbas says there were three groups and only the admonishers survived; the quiet group and offenders both perished.
rows.anchor: وروي عنه أيضا أنه قال: (كانوا أثلاثا؛ ثلثا نهى

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd also says three groups existed: the admonishers survived and the offenders and quiet group perished; he calls this the Quran's strongest verse on abandoning the duty to forbid wrong.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن زيد أيضا، قال: (كانوا ثلاث فرق

rows.speaker: ابن جريج عن عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima recounts visiting Ibn Abbas as he wept over the Qur'an and asked what became of the silent group; Ikrima argued that the admonishers' question implied disapproval and that the verse states neither rescue nor destruction for them, persuading Ibn Abbas that they survived.
rows.anchor: دخلت على ابن عباس وهو ينظر في المصحف ويبكي قبل أن يذهب بصره، فقلت: ما يبكيك

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says two groups were saved and one perished: the fishers who took the fish.
rows.anchor: نجت فرقتان، وهلكت فرقة، وهم الذين أخذوا الحيتان

rows.speaker: يمان
rows.claim: Yaman says both the admonishers and those who asked why they admonished were saved, while the disobedient were destroyed.
rows.anchor: وقال يمان: (نجت الطائفتان؛ الذين قالوا: {لم تعظون}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says a later generation of Jews came after the people God had dispersed.
rows.anchor: فخلف من بعد هؤلاء الذين قطعناهم خلف من اليهود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
rows.claim: In Ata's report, Ibn Abbas explains the successors as descendants, the children of those dispersed across the lands.
rows.anchor: وقال في رواية عطاء: (يريد: نسلا منهم)

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says khalaf can mean a generation following another, or something that replaces what was taken; the replacement sense can also be spelled khalaf.
rows.anchor: يقال للقرن الذي يجيء في أثر قرن: خلف، والخلف ما أخلف عليك بدلا مما أخذ منك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra reads khalaf with a quiescent lām as a generation, and khalaf as what one appoints to replace what has gone.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: {خلف} أي: قرن بجزم اللام، والخلف ما استخلفته

rows.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
rows.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya says the common distinction is khalaf with fatḥa for a good successor and sukūn for a bad one; Abu Ubayda also held this, though he alone allowed sukūn for a good successor too.
rows.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى: (الناس كلهم يقولون: خلف صدق وخلف سوء

rows.speaker: الأزهري عن الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Azhari reports al-Farra allowing khalaf with sukūn for both good and bad generations, explaining that it denotes a generation; he says this agrees with Abu Ubayda.
rows.anchor: الخلف يذهب به إلى الذم، والخلف خلف صالح، وقد يكون في الرديء خلف وفي الصالح خلف

rows.speaker: حسان
rows.claim: Hassan's verse uses khalaf with a quiescent lām for righteous successors, supporting the permissive usage.
rows.anchor: ينشد لحسان: لنا القدم الأولى عليهم وخلفنا

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit says one uses khalaf ṣidq and khalaf sūʾ, with the form unchanged for singular and plural, and cites poetry for the pejorative form.
rows.anchor: يقال: هذا خلف صدق، وهذا خلف سوء، وهؤلاء خلف سوء

rows.speaker: أصحاب العربية
rows.claim: The grammarians derive pejorative khalaf from corruption, citing the idiom nṭaqa khalfan for bad speech and khalafa for spoiled wine or a foul-smelling mouth.
rows.anchor: الخلف المستعمل في الذم مأخوذ من الخلف، وهو الفساد

rows.speaker: النضر
rows.claim: Al-Nadr allows both vowelings for a bad generation but only fatḥa for a good one; most lexicographers agree, except al-Farra and Abu Ubayda, who allow sukūn for the good.
rows.anchor: الخلف بتحريك اللام وإسكانها في القرن السوء واحد، فأما في القرن الصالح فتحريك اللام لا غير

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd distinguishes ʿaraḍ with fatḥa as all worldly goods from ʿarḍ with sukūn as goods other than coined gold and silver; the latter is pluralized as ʿurūḍ.
rows.anchor: جميع متاع الدنيا عرض بفتح الراء، يقال: إن الدنيا عرض حاضر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says they took whatever temptation appeared, lawful or unlawful, including bribes and similar gains.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1): (يأخذون الطمع إذا عرض لهم حلالا

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ata's report from Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as whatever worldly benefit presented itself to them.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عنه: (يريد: ما أشرف لهم من الدنيا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Adnā is a masculine adjective for al-dunyā: the feminine noun for this worldly abode is omitted, leaving its adjective masculine.
rows.anchor: و {الأدنى} تذكير (الدنيا) وأراد عرض هذه الدار الدنيا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators condemn Jews who inherited, read, and learned scripture but abandoned its practice and rulings, taking bribes in judgment and altering the Book and the Messenger's description.
rows.anchor: المفسرون: (ذم الله تعالى بهذه الآية اليهود {ورثوا الكتاب} فقرؤوه، وعلموه، وضيعوا (¬6) العمل به
